Entertainment.title: WIND AND SEA Teams Up With 'Ultraman' for a Capsule Collection
Entertainment.text: SummaryWIND AND SEA partners with Ultraman for a nostalgic collaborative capsule.The drop features heavyweight hoodies, tees, and monster graphics starring actor Shiro Sano.Dropping October 31, 2026, online and across flagship stores.One of Japan's most enduring pop culture heroes is getting a streetwear makeover as WIND AND SEA joins forces with Ultraman for a collaborative capsule.First introduced by Tsuburaya Productions in 1966, Ultraman has become a defining fixture of Japanese science-fiction entertainment, recognized for its towering silver-and-red hero, extraterrestrial adversaries and elaborate monster designs. The partnership arrives during the franchise's 60th anniversary year, offering an apparel-focused interpretation of its visual legacy while connecting nostalgic television imagery with WIND AND SEA's contemporary streetwear identity.The collection merges classic kaiju and superhero lore with WIND AND SEA’s signature typography and relaxed streetwear silhouettes. Across the lineup, heavyweight graphic hoodies, crewneck sweatshirts, long-sleeve shirts, and casual tees showcase archival imagery of Ultraman alongside iconic kaiju monsters and co-branded retro emblems. Rendered with vintage poster-style prints, distressed finishes, and bold color blocking, each garment reinterprets the vibrant special-effects visuals of 1960s and 70s Japanese television into versatile, daily wardrobe staples.Reinforcing the cultural narrative and authenticity of the project, the campaign teaser prominently features acclaimed Japanese actor Shiro Sano- widely recognized as a passionate, lifelong devotee of the Ultraman series - bridging vintage science-fiction fandom with modern Tokyo street culture.The WIND AND SEA x Ultraman capsule collection is set to release on October 31, 2026, and will be available online via the WIND AND SEA official webstore, across the brand’s flagship retail doors in Tokyo and Osaka, alongside select authorized stockists. View this post on Instagram A post shared by WIND AND SEA (@windandsea_wear)Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: WACKO MARIA and Champion Reimagine Reverse Weave Classics for Their First Collaboration
Entertainment.text: SummaryWACKO MARIA and Champion unite for their first Reverse Weave capsule.The five-style collection features heavyweight fleece, TIM LEHI artwork and bold graphics.Launching October 31, the range includes sweatshirts, hoodies and sweatpants in multiple colorways.Champion's iconic Reverse Weave sweatshirt gets a rebellious makeover as the American sportswear label joins forces with WACKO MARIA for their first collaborative capsule.The collaboration centers on Reverse Weave, Champion's signature construction method developed in the 1930s to minimize shrinkage by cutting fleece fabric horizontally rather than vertically. Reinforced with expansion gussets along the sides, the technique has become synonymous with the brand's durable sweatshirts, providing a familiar foundation for WACKO MARIA's more graphic-driven aesthetic.The five-style capsule comprises a crewneck sweatshirt, two pullover hoodies, a full-zip hoodie and matching sweatpants, all constructed from heavyweight 11.5 oz cotton-blend terry fleece. Leading the assortment is a crewneck featuring subtle embroidery at the chest and a striking back graphic created by tattoo artist TIM LEHI, a longtime collaborator of WACKO MARIA. Available in Silver Grey, Black, Amber Brown, Light Blue and Light Pink, the piece introduces the broadest color palette of the collection.The remaining styles adopt a more restrained Silver Grey and Black offering, allowing their contrasting graphics to take center stage. One pullover hoodie displays an oversized WACKO MARIA graphic across the front, while another pairs co-branded chest embroidery with a prominent “Wacko Maria Paradise” print on the back. The full-zip hoodie follows a similar design language with a bold rear graphic, complemented by relaxed sweatpants featuring embroidered branding at the thigh and ribbed cuffs. Across the range, WACKO MARIA's original patterns and Champion's archival-inspired blue single-color neck labels, referencing its 1970s designs, add further character to the familiar athletic silhouettes.The WACKO MARIA x Champion Reverse Weave collection is scheduled to launch on October 31, 2026, at 12 p.m. JST through Champion's official Japanese online store, Champion Harajuku and Champion Brand House Shinsaibashi Osaka, alongside WACKO MARIA's own stores, online platform and select retailers.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Fender and Dark Horse Records Introduce Three Custom George Harrison Stratocasters
Entertainment.text: SummaryFender and Dark Horse Records celebrate George Harrison's legacy with a Japan-exclusive collection.Highlights include three custom Stratocasters andcollectible accessories.The collection features archival Dark Horse graphics, Japanese craftsmanship and Harrison-inspired designs.George Harrison's creative legacy takes on a new form as Fender joins forces with Dark Horse Records for a Japan-exclusive collection spanning musical instruments and accessories. Celebrating the late Beatles guitarist's influence beyond music, the collaboration draws inspiration from his personal style, artistic independence and the visual identity of Dark Horse Records, the label he founded in 1974.Harrison's longstanding relationship with Japan, particularly his celebrated 1991 tour of the country, provides a fitting backdrop for the project, which also coincides with the Year of the Horse in 2026. Bringing together Fender's instrument-making heritage and the Japanese craftsmanship of its lifestyle imprint F Is For Fender, the collection reinterprets archival imagery and recognizable Dark Horse motifs across a range of contemporary designs.Leading the release is the George Harrison Dark Horse Records Stratocaster, available in Olympic White, Black and Orange. Each guitar features custom Dark Horse graphics, gold hardware and an engraved neck plate, pairing the classic Stratocaster silhouette with artwork referencing Harrison's independent record label. The instrument is constructed with an alder body, maple Modern “C” neck and rosewood fingerboard, alongside three Player Series Alnico 5 single-coil pickups and a two-point synchronized tremolo.Complementing the guitar is a limited-edition strap featuring textured-grain detailing and Dark Horse artwork, as well as a collectible set of 12 uniquely designed picks housed in a matching tin. The lineup also includes the existing Dhani Harrison Signature Ukulele, extending the creative connection between Fender and the Harrison family.The Fender x Dark Horse Records collection began rolling out in Japan on October 16, 2026, with availability varying across products. The Stratocaster retails for ¥198,000 JPY (approx. $1,320 USD), while the limited-edition strap and pick set are priced at ¥10,450 JPY (approx. $70 USD) and ¥3,850 JPY (approx. $26 USD), respectively. Entertainment.title: Brabus Reveals the P900 Rocket Edition, a 900 HP G 63 Pickup Truck Limited to 10 Units Worldwide
Entertainment.text: SummaryBrabus has transformed the Mercedes-AMG G 63 into a 900-horsepower custom pickup truckThe coachbuilt conversion replaces the enclosed SUV shape with an open cargo bed and an aggressive carbon-fiber widebodyProduction of the highly modified vehicle is strictly capped at just 10 units worldwideThe Mercedes-Benz G-Wagen operates as a highly audacious luxury status symbol straight from the dealership, but aftermarket heavyweights at Brabus pushed that ostentatious appeal into entirely new territory. Tuning house Brabus officially introduced the Brabus P900 Rocket Edition, a custom pickup truck based on the W 465 series Mercedes-AMG G 63. By completely rethinking the vehicle's architecture, this ultra-limited pickup conversion explicitly targets wealthy buyers in hyper-visible markets like Los Angeles and Miami who wish to stand out far beyond the footprint of a conventional SUV. Production of the highly modified truck is strictly limited to 10 units worldwide, ensuring absolute exclusivity on the streets.To create the imposing silhouette, the standard enclosed SUV shape is entirely replaced by an open rear cargo bed. The Brabus P900 Rocket Edition demands attention through an adapted, exposed carbon-fiber ROCKET EDITION WIDESTAR design. Visually, the exterior is styled with aggressive red accents that pop against the carbon weave, and the entire chassis sits on massive 24-inch BRABUS Monoblock II EVO wheels.Under the hood, the engineering overhaul is just as radical as the aesthetic transformation. Brabus increased the displacement of the standard Mercedes-Benz 4.0-liter V-8 engine up to 4.5 liters. This heavily modified 4.5-liter twin-turbo V8 engine now produces a staggering 900 horsepower, or 662 kW. That output represents a significant increase over the standard G63's already potent 577 horsepower. The newly expanded engine also generates a massive peak torque output of 922 lb-ft (1250 Nm). However, that brute force is electronically limited at 774 lb-ft purely to protect the vehicle's essential drivetrain components from the overwhelming twist.Performance metrics are staggering for a vehicle of this size and shape. The custom pickup truck accelerates from 0 to 62 miles per hour (100 km/h) in a blistering 3.7 seconds. That sprint time is a full seven-tenths of a second quicker than the manufacturer's official claim for the standard G63. Top speed is electronically limited to 149 mph (240 km/h). Moving that much metal at those speeds requires serious fuel consumption, and the P900 Rocket Edition registers a combined fuel economy rating of 17.3 liters per 100 kilometers, alongside CO2 emissions of 393 g/km.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Science & Technology.title: Build a Hidden Lock With a Magnetic Imager
Science & Technology.text: Like many a nerd, I have a certain fascination with locks. This originates in reading the memoir Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman as a teenager, in which Richard Feynman recounts picking locks and cracking combinations while at his day job working on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos. I currently have a couple of locksport pick sets and training locks that I purchased at hacker conferences over the years (although I’m still terrible at it), and I delight in the YouTube exploits of folks like the LockPickingLawyer.All of which left me wondering if I could try building an interesting lock. One dodge that lockmakers have long used to challenge would-be plunderers is to conceal the existence of the lock itself. A modern variant of this is the magnetic lock, where a magnet is held or slid against an innocuous portion of a door or box, releasing a catch. The problem with this is that, once you guess the location of the lock, any strong magnet will open it.So I started thinking about embedding an RFID reader under the surface and resigning myself to keeping track of yet another access card. But then I stumbled across something much more interesting: SparkFun’s US $100 magnetic imaging tile. I realized I could use this to build a magnetic lock that opens with a programmable secret gesture.  I used a few discrete components to drive the servo motor and put the lock into program mode [top], controlled by a Teensy 4.1 microcontroller [middle]. An array of Hall-effect sensors detect magnetic fields [bottom].James ProvostThe magnetic imaging tile is a small-run SparkFun board based on the work of Peter Jansen. It features an 8-by-8 grid of Hall-effect sensors, and uses an SPI interface to talk to the microcontroller of your choice. These sensors can detect both the magnitude and polarity of a magnetic field, and the board can report its measurements hundreds to thousands of times per second, depending on how much processing power your microcontroller has available. This is easily fast enough to capture the motion of a magnet being moved by hand across the board’s sensor area—my secret gesture.An interesting thing about using magnetic fields is that if I was in extreme paranoia mode, I could shield the entire lock behind copper sheeting, something I couldn’t do with an RFID reader. The copper sheet would act as a Faraday cage, blocking any RFID signal, along with any other electromagnetic fields an attacker with an EMF meter might use to locate the lock.Choosing the Brains of the BoxI chose a Teensy 4.1 as my microcontroller. I like the Teensy because it offers loads of input/output, a 600-megahertz processor, a megabyte of RAM, and a built-in SD card, all in a slim package with an equally slim $32 price tag.Wiring the Teensy to the magnetic-imaging tile was trivial, only complicated by the fact that one side of the board has a silk-screen error that misidentifies the SPI connections (SparkFun says this will be fixed in future runs of the board).In extreme paranoia mode, I could shield the entire lock behind copper sheeting.To create the gesture-recognition software, I once again turned to vibe coding. If you read my Hands On piece in the April 2026 issue of IEEE Spectrum on creating a teletext suite for ham radio, you’ll know I’ve been grappling with how vibe coding should be used in DIY projects, if at all. So this time, instead of letting Claude write all the software, I confined it to writing just two support libraries, which you can find in our online repository at https://github.com/IEEESpectrumHandsOn.One library is in charge of recording a lock gesture and saving it to the Teensy’s nonvolatile storage. The other library monitors the tile and reports whether or not a newly detected gesture passes a selectable threshold to be considered a match.I wrote the top-level code myself to keep it as DIY as possible. This code handles things like a button that puts the system in gesture-recording mode after a brief delay, the indicator LED for recording mode, and the code that operates the physical locking mechanism.  Hall-effect sensors rely on a current passing through a p-type slab of silicon. A magnetic field passing through the silicon deflects charge carriers toward the edges of the slab, creating a voltage proportional to the field [left]. By looking at the intensities of the voltages across an 8-by-8 grid of sensors, the microcontroller can reconstruct a gesture [right]. James ProvostOf course, I needed something to lock to demonstrate my proof of concept. I bought a wooden craft box and removed the existing lid latch. I glued a notched beam inside the lid and built a mechanism that uses a servo motor to rotate another beam in and out of this notch. I will be the first to admit this mechanism goes beyond “simple” and into “simplistic,” but it’s sufficiently robust for my demo. The box has ample room for the magnetic imaging tile to be mounted against one wall, along with the Teensy and other supporting electronics. These include a battery pack, the recording button, and a small additional board with two NPN transistors. These convert the Teensy’s 3.3-volt control signals to a 5-V signal needed to drive the servo.Once it was all put together, I soon discovered that the small size of the magnetic tile’s sensing area—just 3 centimeters square—made it easy to fit the tile inside the box but hard to do the unlock gesture on the outside so that it is read correctly. Marking the outline of the sensor area on the outside defeated the point of having a hidden lock, so instead I once again turned to mining my Irish heritage. I created a Celtic knotwork pattern that runs in a band across the front of the lockbox (I used an online knotwork generator and then projected and traced the pattern onto the box). Using the pattern as a camouflaged reference grid I can make a repeatable gesture within the confines of the sensor area. (To make the gestures I’m using a magnetic stylus borrowed from a ferrite core-memory kit we featured in 2022.)There’s obvious room for improvement in any more serious installation. The biggest drawback currently is that if the box is locked when the battery runs out, you can’t open it again without breaking something. This could be solved by adding a hidden inductive charging coil. Nonetheless, the demo lockbox works well—now I just have to think what I should store in it!

Science & Technology.title: Apple’s iPad mini Finally Gets OLED and Water Resistance
Science & Technology.text: SummaryApple has redesigned the iPad mini with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, an IP67 rating and a 5.4 mm profileThe new A20 Pro chip delivers up to 4.5x faster AI performance and up to 2.7x faster graphics than the previous generationAn Acoustic Display, a landscape front camera and Apple’s N1 and C2 connectivity chips round out the overhaulApple has unveiled the all-new iPad mini, a top-to-bottom redesign that brings an 8.5-inch OLED display, IP67 water and dust resistance and the 2-nanometer A20 Pro chip to its smallest tablet. Apple is calling it the biggest update in the iPad mini’s history, and the spec sheet backs that up, with upgrades touching nearly every part of the device, from its audio and cameras to its wireless connectivity.The chassis is the first thing to shrink. At just 5.4 mm thick, the new iPad mini is both slimmer and lighter than its predecessor, and it now carries an IP67 rating, which Apple tested for submersion up to 1 meter for 30 minutes. That means a rainy commute or a poolside read no longer has to be a gamble. Two finishes are on offer, a new midnight and starlight, with storage configurations of 128GB, 256GB and 512GB.The display has grown without the tablet getting any bigger. Bezels that are 24 percent thinner make room for an 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR screen in the same footprint as before, and the switch to OLED brings pixel-level lighting control for much deeper blacks, a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio and P3 wide color support. Peak brightness hits up to 1,200 nits, more than double the last model, with 600 nits of full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content. At the other end, a 1-nit minimum makes it easier on the eyes in a dark bedroom or a cockpit. For the first time on iPad mini, buyers can also opt for a nano-texture finish to cut glare outdoors, a feature previously reserved for iPad Pro.Under the hood, A20 Pro is built on Apple’s 2-nanometer process and uses a new package that borrows from the company’s M-series chips. Its 7-core GPU puts a Neural Accelerator in every core, pushing AI performance up to 4.5x higher than the previous generation, while dynamic caching, mesh shading and hardware-accelerated ray tracing lift graphics performance by up to 2.7x. A CPU with up to six cores adds up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance, and unified memory bandwidth more than doubles. The 512GB model goes a step further with a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, giving it 32 cores and twice the processing power of its predecessor for heavier on-device AI workloads.Audio gets a rethink too. Apple’s new Acoustic Display routes purpose-built woofers through the screen for louder, punchier bass, while custom tweeters are tucked between the glass and the aluminum shell to sharpen the highs. The sealed speaker enclosure also plays a part in achieving the IP67 rating. On the camera front, the 12MP Center Stage front camera has moved to the landscape edge for more natural video calls, and the 12MP Wide rear camera shoots 4K video at up to 60 fps, now paired with an Adaptive True Tone flash for better photos and document scans.Connectivity rounds out the hardware story. Apple’s N1 wireless chip brings Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread to the iPad mini for the first time, while cellular models use the C2 modem for up to 50 percent faster data speeds and better power efficiency. The tablet ships with iPadOS 27, including a beta of Siri AI, Apple’s rebuilt, Apple Intelligence-powered assistant, along with support for extended display mode once iPadOS 27.2 arrives.All of that is aimed at an audience that has always used the mini differently from other iPads. “iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.”A redesigned Smart Folio arrives alongside the tablet, with a two-panel magnetic build in TechWoven fabric offered in navy blue and taupe and an adjustable design that unlocks new viewing angles. The iPad mini also supports both Apple Pencil Pro and Apple Pencil (USB-C).The new iPad mini opens for pre-order on Wednesday, October 28, via Apple and the Apple Store app in 36 countries and regions. It arrives at Apple Store locations and Apple Authorized Resellers on Friday, November 6.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Artificial Intelligence.title: IEEE Xplore Digital Library Adds AI Assistant
Artificial Intelligence.text: IEEE recently released the IEEE Xplore AI Research Suite, built on the full text of millions of peer-reviewed publications in the IEEE Xplore Digital Library. The library offers full-text access to IEEE standards, journals, magazines, conference proceedings, and more.Researchers who use the AI suite to search the digital library receive answers grounded in verified scientific results, ensuring a high level of accuracy and trust.The suite is available as an optional subscription upgrade to all IEEE Xplore Digital Library institutional subscribers.Powered by a proprietary AI system optimized for STEM literature, the suite introduces powerful, intelligent features within the digital library. The suite enables users to seamlessly search and discover articles to accelerate their comprehension of complex technical papers.The system surfaces deep insights, replacing the typical keyword queries with natural, conversational research workflows.As AI tools become more common in conducting research, IEEE collaborated to build the suite around a simple principle: Answers should be trustworthy, not just fast, says W. Clem Karl, vice president, IEEE Publication Services and Products.“AI can be a highly effective and beneficial tool that can help researchers accelerate discovery, enhance decision-making, and surface new connections,” Karl says. “However, many AI engines present a great risk of hallucinating answers or introducing bias into otherwise credible research. With this in mind, IEEE has taken a responsible approach in our AI strategy by developing concrete safeguards to ensure our solution is rigorously grounded in scientific evidence that users can trust.“As stewards of the scholarly record, we held the new AI engine to the same standards as the peer-reviewed research we publish: A researcher shouldn’t have to trust an answer; they should be able to verify the work behind it.”Collaboration with the scientific communityThe IEEE Xplore AI Research Suite was developed in close collaboration with global scientific and library communities.The development process began with research into user needs and the challenges associated with existing AI research assistants. More than 3,000 testers—including engineers, scientists, and library information professionals—provided feedback to refine the AI engine and support research workflows.Capabilities include: Semantic AI search. Users can input free-form, natural-language queries or paste long blocks of text to locate similar research and identify novel solutions.Time-saving summaries. The platform generates immediate, accurate AI overviews of search results and provides in-context definitions of technical terms so that users can grasp new concepts faster and accelerate their research.Built on trusted content. The suite is the only AI research assistant that uses both the full text and metadata of IEEE’s peer-reviewed journal articles and conference papers to optimize the accuracy and relevance of the results.Comprehensive coverage. A variety of STEM metadata is available from journal articles and conference papers that have been curated to include scholarly articles without the typical noise found in other tools.Source links and verifiable results. The AI-generated overviews include reference links to source documents, allowing users to verify information and cross-reference findings.Reducing hallucinationsTo mitigate the risk of AI hallucinations, the search-retrieval process is limited to querying the millions of IEEE peer-reviewed full-text documents, alongside an expertly curated dataset of STEM metadata. If the AI tool is unable to find relevant scientific content within the defined dataset, it is designed to inform the user rather than generate fabricated answers.“IEEE is committed to providing the technical community with a highly precise and reliable research experience,” says Steven Heffner, IEEE’s chief publication officer and managing director of IEEE Publications. “The IEEE Xplore AI Research Suite offers something unique in that it is the only AI research assistant that leverages both the full-text and metadata of IEEE’s peer-reviewed content, rather than abstracts alone.“The difference is significant: Our internal testing showed a threefold increase in result quality and accuracy across every key metric. These results underscore how critical full-text grounding is for technical research.”For more information about features and coverage, or to request a demo for your organization, visit the IEEE Xplore AI Research Suite website.

Rather than presenting nature literally, the boutique hints at it - a wash of green here, a hazy reflection there - creating the sense of a garden remembered rather than directly recreated.At its center sits the Scent Altar, where softly illuminated forms partially conceal the fragrances within, encouraging discovery through curiosity instead of immediately revealing every bottle.
